icp: B2B product used by engineering/platform teams to build or operate developer infrastructure such as CI/CD, observability, APIs, cloud infrastructure, or internal platforms. General productivity, design, CRM, and collaboration software alone do not qualify.

cases.gold_rationale: The frozen description explicitly identifies CircleCI as a CI/CD product used by engineering teams to validate code and deliver software. CI/CD is directly named in the ICP as developer infrastructure, and the evidence clearly describes the product as serving that function.

The frozen description identifies Datadog as a monitoring platform for cloud applications that provides observability across servers, containers, databases, and third-party services. It explicitly describes DevOps teams using the product to operate and troubleshoot their systems, directly matching the observability and cloud-infrastructure portions of the ICP.

The frozen description centers HubSpot on marketing, sales, service, website management, and customer engagement. Although the company is categorized as Software Development, the evidence does not show that its primary product is used by engineering or platform teams to build or operate developer infrastructure. CRM and related customer-platform software are explicitly outside the ICP on their own.

The frozen description presents Canva as a visual communications and design platform built around templates, drag-and-drop creation, and making design accessible. The evidence does not indicate that the product is used to build or operate developer infrastructure. Design software is explicitly outside the ICP on its own.

The frozen description presents Notion as an all-in-one workspace for product roadmaps, company wikis, meeting notes, and customizable team workflows. While engineering teams could use some of these workflows, the evidence describes a general productivity and collaboration product rather than infrastructure used to build or operate software systems. General productivity and collaboration software alone do not qualify under the ICP.

The frozen description presents Linear as an issue-tracking and project-management tool for product teams building software. This gives it a clear engineering and software-development adjacency, but the evidence does not establish that Linear itself is developer infrastructure such as CI/CD, observability, APIs, cloud infrastructure, or an internal platform. It therefore fits more closely than general productivity software while stopping short of a direct infrastructure match.
